Zul'Aman (/ˈzuːl əˌmɔn/ ZOOL-ə-mawn) is a fortress and a temple city that serves as the capital of the Amani tribe, located in the southeastern portion of Quel'Thalas, on northern Lordaeron. The main temple area is known as Atal'Aman.
It was revisited as a zone in World of Warcraft: Midnight.

The main temple area is known as [[Atal'Aman]]. It was revisited as a zone in ''[[World of Warcraft: Midnight]]''. ==History== ===Founding=== [[File:Zul'Aman overview.jpg|thumb|Zul'Aman in ''World of Warcraft''.]] During the [[Aqir and Troll War]] circa 16,000 [[BDP]],{{Ref WoWCV1|70|74}} atop the site where the [[Zandalari]] and their allies had killed the [[C'Thrax]] [[Kith'ix]], they established a new settlement which would one day grow into a sprawling temple city known as Zul'Aman.{{Ref WoWCV1|72|73}} ===Empire's Fall=== By the time of the [[Troll Wars]] in 2,600 BDP, the [[Amani Empire]] in Zul'Aman was the most powerful empire in the [[Eastern Kingdoms]].[[The Founding of Quel'Thalas]] The [[high elf|high elves]] of [[Quel'Thalas (kingdom)|Quel'Thalas]] eventually joined with the [[human]]s of the [[Arathor|Empire of Arathor]] in an immense battle that signaled the end of the forest trolls' empire. The Amani would never recover enough to extend their land beyond their home province of Zul'Aman, but they continued to be an enemy of humans and elves for thousands of years.[[Arathor and the Troll Wars]] [[Silvermoon City]] itself was constructed over the site of sacred [[troll]] grounds, burial grounds of the [[Hash'ey]] [[Atal'Kindo]], which earned the elves further enmity from the neighboring [[Amani tribe]].''[[Ultimate Visual Guide]]'', pg. 148 ===Second War=== [[File:Alliance of Lordaeron besieging Zul'Aman.jpg|thumb|Zul'Aman besieged by the [[Alliance of Lordaeron]].]] During the [[Second War]] in 6 [[ADP]], [[Zul'jin]] and the Amani joined the [[Old Horde|Orcish Horde]], while the high elves joined the [[Alliance of Lordaeron]]. The Warlord of Zul'Aman eventually disappeared mysteriously after the [[orc]]s were defeated.[[Cannibalistic Cousins]] In truth, Zul'jin had been captured and tortured by the [[Farstriders]], and retreated into Zul'Aman to recuperate after an Amani war party saved him. ===Fall of Zul'jin=== {{bc-section}} During the [[invasion of Outland]] in 26 ADP, [[Zul'jin]] saw the opportunity to take revenge against Quel'Thalas when most of the [[Blood elf|blood elves]] and [[Horde]] were busy fighting in [[Outland]]. Not wanting to fight a war on two fronts, the Horde sent a task force of some of their strongest champions to kill the [[Amani tribe|Amani]] leadership within Zul'Aman.{{Ref WoWCV3|325}} At the entrance to the city, the adventurers encountered [[Budd Nedreck]], who convinced them to also steal the treasures within as well. ===Cataclysm=== {{cata-section}} [[File:Zul'AmanPreparationConversation.jpg|thumb|The elves and trolls reunion at the [[Amani Pass]].]] With [[Zul'jin]] dead, the halls of Zul'Aman become quiet until the [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]] in 28 ADP. With the aid of the [[Zandalari]], the remaining Amani united under the leadership of [[Daakara|Warlord Daakara]], who sought to avenge Zul'jin's death and realize his dreams of rebuilding the troll empire.[http://us.battle.net/wow/en/blog/2514161#blog Patch 4.1 Content Preview: Rise of the Zandalari] When all tribes were invited to become a part of this new empire, [[Vol'jin]] of the [[Darkspear tribe|Darkspear]] declined this offer, and instead joined forces with the [[Farstriders]] and [[Silver Covenant]]. Along with [[Halduron Brightwing]] and [[Vereesa Windrunner]], he could be found planning their next move on the outskirts of Zul'Aman.Leaders' meeting at the [[Zul'Aman#Amani Pass|Amani Pass]] Heroes of the [[Alliance]] and the [[Horde]] eventually entered Zul'Aman and thwarted the Zandalari plans by killing Daakara.[[Warlord of the Amani]] ===Midnight=== {{Mn-section}} During the [[War of Light and Shadow]], the [[Twilight's Blade]] launched an incursion into Zul'Aman. To combat their Void magics, [[Zul'jan]] led the [[Amani tribe]] into [[Eversong Woods]] to harvest [[Lightwood]] to craft weapons.[[A Foe Unseen]] They were driven back by the blood elves and the [[Vanguard of the Light]],[[Light Guide Us]] but lingered at the [[Amani Pass]] to eventually resume their operations.[[The Gates of Zul'Aman]] [[Zul'jarra]] arrived at the Pass to reinforce her brother,[[The Line Must Be Drawn Here]] but after the costly battle against the blood elves, they did not have the strength to defend [[Atal'Aman]] from the Twilight's Blade, resulting in it being captured.[[Isolation]] To defeat the Blade, Zul'jarra decided to become a [[hash'ey]] to bring back the aid of the loa.[[The Path of the Amani]] While she journeyed across Zul'Aman to garner favor with the various loa, Zul'jan led the Amani warriors into another costly battle to reclaim their Lightwood.[[Den of Nalorakk: A Taste of Vengeance]] Despite being scolded by his sister, he once more led their forces to drive out the Twilight's Blade. Though initially overwhelmed, Zul'jarra came with reinforcements from the loa and other Amani tribes. Together, they killed [[Mor'duun]] and weakened the cult's presence in Zul'Aman.[[Blade Shattered]] ==Geography== ===Maps and subregions=== [[File:WorldMap-NewZulAman.jpg|thumb|Zone map in ==In the RPG== {{RPG-section}} The [[forest troll]] [[kingdom]] of Zul'Aman is a dark, primal woodland and the only place of life in the [[Blackened Woods|Ghostlands]] of [[Quel'Thalas]]. The [[troll]]s' [[voodoo]] energies permeate the climate, and ancient, stepped ziggurats rise above the canopy. [[Jin'zakk|Warlord Jin'zakk]] is rumored to command the trolls, and his [[witch doctor]]s and [[shaman]]s provide him with [[magic]] support.''[[World of Warcraft: The Roleplaying Game]]'', pg. 22 ===History=== Once, forest trolls controlled a vast swath of [[Lordaeron]]. Their empire was called [[Amani Empire|Zul'Aman]], and the area currently known as Zul'Aman was their power center. Their dominion stretched across the continent, and they threatened the nascent [[human nation]]s and the fledgling [[Quel'Thalas (kingdom)|kingdom of Quel'Thalas]] with extinction. Eventually, the [[High elf|high elves]] traded [[arcane]] knowledge to the [[human]]s for help in defeating the trolls, and the two races bludgeoned the forest troll empire. Now, this tiny area in northeastern Lordaeron is all that remains of the trolls' continent-spanning empire. In the years after their defeat, the trolls largely gave up their imperialist mindset, though they protect their small territory zealously. They have never forgiven the humans or the elves for their near-genocide. Warbands patrol the forest, slaying all living and [[undead]] creatures that are not trolls or natural forest beasts. They worship ancient deities, though whether these deities are the mythic [[Old Gods]] or some strange creation of their voodoo witch doctors is unknown. With [[Lordaeron (kingdom)|Lordaeron]] and Quel'Thalas in ruins, the trolls move out to reclaim their kingdom.''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 115''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 118 Any trolls encountered try to kill on sight. Explorers need to be careful but are not totally without allies in Zul'Aman. Several bands of high elves, survivors from Quel'Thalas, fled south and now wander throughout the forest. Those who stay one step ahead of the trolls survive; those who do not will learn first-hand what the cannibalistic trolls do with their victims. [[Scourge]] patrols, hunting the elven refugees, also stalk through the land. The Scourge group in Zul'Aman is led by [[Ru'sad|Necromancer Ru'sad]], and they are having difficulties trying to end the elves as they know the forests better than the undead. Incorporeal troops such as [[shades]] or [[ghost]]s would be more helpful as the [[ghoul]]s and [[zombie]]s make a fearsome amount of noise trudging through the overgrowth alerting the elves. The [[gargoyle]]s are somewhat more useful; they fly through the clearings and dense tangles of the jungle and allow the undead to discover refugee groups which they later kill as they sleep. The Scourge are confident that it is only a matter of time before they finally destroy all of the elves. They intend to prevent them from joining with their allies in [[Hillsbrad Foothills|Hillsbrad]] or [[Khaz Modan]], or rally together. They intend to stop them from reviving the [[Sunwell]].''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 117 A great witch doctor, [[Ral'jin]], rose to prominence in Zul'Aman. Ral'jin sent out [[hunter]]s to capture hundreds of prisoners for use in a massive sacrifice, planning to use this ritual to summon [[Ula-Tek]], the Serpent Goddess. This information is bad news, but the [[Ironforge (kingdom)|Ironforge]] [[Dwarf|dwarves]] are particularly concerned: they have seen the devastation that an [[Elemental Lord|elemental lord]]'s rebirth brings, and a bona fide [[Old God]] must be even more powerful. The [[Dark Iron clan|Dark Iron dwarves]], however, are jubilant. Ula-Tek, perhaps an Old God, could serve as a companion and ally to [[Ragnaros]]. The Dark Iron sent a contingent to Zul'Aman to wish their goodwill and to protect Ral'jin as he completes the lengthy ritual. ===Culture=== [[File:Zul'AmanLOC.JPG|thumb|Zul'Aman in ''[[Lands of Conflict]]''.]] Forest trolls are vile creatures. They practice evil voodoo magic and worship primal beings they call the Forest Gods. Violent cannibals, forest trolls eat their own kind as well as their enemies with equal zest. The trolls joined forces with the Horde in the Second War, as the orcs promised them vengeance against Lordaeron and Quel'Thalas, but the trolls' savagery was too much even for the orcs. Due to this, the trolls also hate orcs now, who they feel betrayed them. In short, forest trolls hate everyone — including each other.''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 115 - 116 Witch doctors control Zul'Aman, with [[shaman]]s and warchiefs in lesser leadership positions. The exception to this tradition is [[Jin'zakk|Warlord Jin'zakk]], who rules the entire kingdom. The voodoo witch doctors wield arcane magic, while shamans provide divine support. Forest troll society revolves around hunting, spear fishing, shamanism, and voodoo. They make their capital at the [[Shrine of Ula-Tek]], a massive ziggurat they hold sacred. Forest troll society is patriarchal, though cunning and aggressive females occasionally hold important positions. Forest trolls are primitive, possessing few metalsmithing skills and no knowledge of steam technology though they are masters with thrown weapons, be they axes or spears. With both Lordaeron and Quel'Thalas fallen, the forest trolls see a chance to regain their old empire. They push the borders of their realm ever outward. Warbands strike south, north and west, seeking to reclaim more of their land. The trolls are myriad — almost 20.000 total, and most of them skilled hunters. They have been fighting for centuries and are competent tacticians. Alone, Zul'Aman has little chance against the Scourge. However, if approached in the right manner (by a tauren or goblin, perhaps) and promised their empire, they may be willing to join an alliance. Like all trolls, Zul'Aman's forest trolls are lean, strong and tough. They possess long ears and noses and jutting canines. Their faces are hard and feral. Forest troll hide ranges from dark brown to light green. Many forest trolls wear primitive jewelry, often wood or bone, on their clothing, strung around their necks or thrust through their noses and earlobes. The males often maintain tall, dyed mohawks. Some paint themselves in tattoos. Forest trolls are organized into tribes, with names such as [[Blackleaf tribe|Blackleaf]] and [[Treeblight tribe|Treeblight]], and members of the same tribe are relatively loyal to each other.''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 116 ===Geography=== Zul'Aman is a temperate forestland of towering trees, dark shadows, and ancient ruins and ziggurats. These ruins and odd, stepped pyramids remain from the days of Zul'Aman's empire, but they could be much older, even [[Titan]] or Old God remnants. Elevation rises toward the north, and a hilly region dominates the Quel'Thalas border. The mighty [[Greenrush River]] begins in Zul'Aman's [[Lake Abassi]] and exits the region in the southwest crossing the [[Eastern Plaguelands]] and emptying into [[Darrowmere Lake]]. The [[Maisara Hills]] to the northeast, are sacred to the trolls. Primitive forest troll settlements are scattered throughout the region. Weathered ruins hide among the trees, covered with vines and the dust of ages. Trolls guard treasure and captives, and ancient ruins of indeterminate origins dominate forest clearings. ==Notes and trivia== *After the [[war against the Primalists]], the [[void elf]] [[Riftwalkers]] noticed [[Void]] activity in the northern Eastern Kingdoms, and the trail went cold near Zul'Aman.[[Riftwalker Reports]] *[[Benjari Edune]] once ventured deep within the forests of Zul'Aman. *The [[Hatchet Hills]] [[flight path]] is labeled as Zul'Aman. *Early in ''World of Warcraft'' development, the Zul'Aman area was in the game's files. *The ritual to open the gates of Zul'Aman requires several people to hit a [[Strange Gong]] together. ==Speculation== {{Speculation}} *In the [[:File:Kalimdor Chronicle.jpg|map]] from {{Ref WoWCV1}}, Zul'Aman is located right above [[Darrowmere Lake]], rather than in [[Eversong Forest]], implying Zul'Aman might have spanned an extremely large area prior to the [[Great Sundering]]. **This is somewhat "confirmed" with the lore stating that [[Quel'Thalas (kingdom)|Quel'Thalas]] and [[Silvermoon City]] were established on the ruins of sacred troll lands, possibly having once been a part of a massive temple city that spanned all the way from Darrowmere Lake to Quel'Thalas. ===Size discrepancies=== *Some maps showing Azeroth following the Sundering depicted Zul'Aman to be bigger compared to its appearance in the game: **A [[:File:Warcraft III Map - Quel'Thalas & Zul'Aman.jpg|map]] from ''[[Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos|Warcraft III]]'' has a building / temple named Ziggurat (this could be the place of the Zul'Aman instance in the game). In the map, the Zul'Aman term uses the "kingdom" font and not "city" font. It is right above Caer Darrow but since that time, the geography of the Eastern Plaguelands has changed and Zul'Aman is no longer above the lake. **A [[:File:WoWLordaeron.jpg|Lordaeron map]] from the ''[[World of Warcraft: Game Manual]]'' uses zone font instead of city font with [[Maisara Hills]] and [[Shrine of Ula'Tek]] as cities. The Shrine is roughly in the place of the in-game's instance. **A {{Ref WoWCV2}} [[:File:Chronicle2 Map of the Second War.jpg|map]] also presents the red area of the Amani tribe which could be the Zul'Aman area. **The larger area may also be supported by the description from ''[[Blood of the Highborne]]'' where [[Liadrin]] climbed a "remote peak east" of Zul'Aman. Atop of the peak, she saw [[Destroyer#Troll destroyer|troll destroyers]] on the ocean. **The geometry of the in-game Quel'Thalas area actually has the Zul'Aman dungeon fully built outside of the instance, forming a rectangular peninsula [[closed zone|not meant to be viewed]] from the outside. The in-game map of the Eastern Kingdoms picks an arbitrary point near the small lake past the inner gate as the start of the coastline, meaning that the dungeon is not meant to be to scale. However, something like this extra area seems to exist on the old maps listed above. ** The in-game map of the Eastern Kingdoms is mostly replicated in {{Ref WoWCV1}}, but ''Chronicle'' adds a bay that extends to about where Zul'Aman's inner gate should be, while expanding the coast of the Eastern Plaguelands slightly. **The map from ''[[Exploring Azeroth: The Eastern Kingdoms]]'' reduces the area east of the Ghostlands ever further, but moves the mountains around [[Zul'Mashar]] further south, which expands the area overall. **''World of Warcraft: Midnight'' goes back to the large peninsula seen on old maps, though divided into two segments by an ocean channel.
